subtopicTitle: Viscous flow — Poiseuille flow, velocity profile in pipe

cards.back: Steady, laminar, fully developed flow of an incompressible Newtonian fluid through a straight circular pipe driven solely by a constant axial pressure gradient.

cards.front: State the no-slip boundary condition for pipe flow of radius R.
cards.back: Axial velocity $u_z(r=R)=0$ (fluid adheres to the wall); symmetry also requires $\partial u_z/\partial r|_{r=0}=0$.

cards.front: Write the radial velocity profile $u_z(r)$ for Poiseuille flow.
cards.back: $u_z(r)=\frac{\Delta P}{4\mu L}(R^2-r^2)$, where $\Delta P>0$ is the pressure drop over length $L$.

cards.front: What is the ratio of average to maximum velocity in Poiseuille pipe flow?

cards.back: Q=\frac{\pi R^4\Delta P}{8\mu L} (or equivalently Q=\frac{\pi R^4}{8\mu}\frac{dp}{dz} with sign).

cards.front: Under what Re condition is Poiseuille flow valid?
cards.back: Re<2300 (laminar regime) where Re=\rho u_{avg}D/\mu; above this transition to turbulence occurs.

cards.front: Derive the axial momentum balance that yields the Poiseuille profile (key steps).
cards.back: Start from incompressible NS in cylindrical coords. For steady, axisymmetric, fully developed flow: (1) all radial/azimuthal velocities=0, (2) \partial/\partial z=0 except for imposed dp/dz, (3) viscous term reduces to \mu(1/r d/dr(r du_z/dr))=dp/dz. Integrate twice and apply BCs to obtain parabolic profile.

cards.front: Obtain wall shear stress \tau_w for Poiseuille flow from the velocity profile.
cards.back: \tau_w=\mu|\partial u_z/\partial r|_{r=R}|=\frac{R\Delta P}{2L}. Force balance on fluid cylinder confirms \tau_w=\frac{R}{2}\frac{dp}{dz}.
